Lane F — finish the reconciliation

Owns: root *.md, AGENTS.md, agents/ Must not touch: computedriven.com/ (lane E), RRABBIT/ (lane A), studbook/ (lane B). Status: ✅ READY NOW. Unblocked, and it clears debt that is actively misleading other sessions.

Why this lane matters more than it looks

On 2026-08-15 CLAUDE.md — the file injected into every session in this tree — was found still teaching the shared-Supabase data layer, with the full migration table and runnable supabase start commands. It had been abandoned sixteen days earlier. Every session in that window began from a false premise.

That is the failure this lane exists to prevent. A ruling that is not swept into the documents is a ruling the next session does not have.

Read first

REVISION_REGISTER.md — the ranked list, with what is fixed and what is not.

Still open

1. STACK_COMPLETION.md §0/§6 — [TRAVIS], not yours

The ratings take Fly deployment breadth as an input, and the wind-down ruling changed it. They are stale, not wrong. The document already reserves the blended-vs-per-layer question for Travis. Flag it; do not recompute it.

2. AGENTS.md is stale and nobody has audited it

Found in passing, never swept: it describes WebHost.Systems as "Convex + Vite/React/Clerk", while CLAUDE.md says Supabase backend + Vite/React/Supabase Auth. One of them is wrong and possibly both. It also predates every 2026-08-15 ruling. 95 lines — read all of it against the tree.

3. The per-product docs/spec/ folders were never swept

~14 of them. WebHost.Systems/docs/spec/30_DATA_MODEL_SUPABASE.md is Supabase by name, and its v1.0 spec is otherwise the most complete hub design in the portfolio. Others certainly assume Supabase or a Fly deployment.

Do not mass-edit. Some of these are dated design records where a supersession banner is the honest fix; others are live guidance that should be corrected. Tell the two apart, and say which you did.

4. Verify ampersand-supabase/ is marked archived

It is archived by decision. Nothing has checked that the directory says so to someone who opens it.

5. Does any live page tell the public it runs on Supabase?

Never checked. Curl the served pages rather than grepping the tree — the local-grep error mode is recorded and has produced a wrong claim here before.

6. Write the threat model — the most valuable thing in this lane

CONFIDENTIALITY.md §1 lists seven adversaries (T1–T7) and none are declared in scope. Every mechanism choice in class B is downstream of that answer. This is a [TRAVIS] ruling, but the document that makes it easy to make — the concrete question, the consequence of each answer — is yours to write.

House rules for this lane specifically

  • Retract in place, by name. Never silently edit a claim away. This tree's retractions are its

most valuable records — the ledger that retracted two of its own findings, the plan that retracted its own pricing twice.

  • Do not rewrite dated analyses. A gap review records what was seen at the time; rewriting it

fabricates a review nobody performed. STACK_ARCHITECTURE_GAP_REVIEW.md, ECOSYSTEM.md and STACK_PLANNING.md got supersession banners for exactly this reason. Say which half survives.

  • Never hand-type a derived number. The law count drifted twice — 116 in four places in

STACK_SITEMAP.md and two more in STACK_COMPLETION.md, where the suites derive 118. The suites count themselves: node test/laws.mjs && node test/compose-laws.mjs from AmpersandBoxDesign/box-and-box/. Quote the output.

  • A boundary in a document is a decision, not a measurement. Plan §8.3's out-of-scope list was

inherited as fact and produced a conclusion off by four orders of magnitude. If a scope looks load-bearing, ask rather than assume.

  • Date every claim, and give it the rung it has earned: spec → in_tree → live_local →

live_deployed → external. When in doubt, downgrade.

Done means

REVISION_REGISTER.md has no open row that is not explicitly [TRAVIS], and each closed row says what was done and how it was checked. Keep the register — it is a standing document, not a one-off. The failure it catches is silent and cumulative.
